newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco stocks end higher, led by blue-chips.
newsitem.headline: Morocco stocks end higher, led by blue-chips.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed on Monday 0.57 percent higher, driven mainly by blue-chip firms such as Banque Commerciale du Maroc, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 575.41 points, up from 572.14 points last Friday.
"The price rise of blue-chip firms was behind the continuing improvement of the bourse index," a market analyst at Casablanca Finance Inermediation said.
The intervention of mutual funds on the bourse also consolidated the market's upward trend, the analysts said. Morocco has more than 24 active mutual funds covering the trading of 47 listed stocks.
"Subscription of the funds was increasing by an average 3.0 percent every week since January...Therefore the share price followed the demand," the analyst added.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market's largest private bank jumped 20 dirhams to 810 dirhams. "BCM's good results are behind the rise," he said.
Wafabank was up five dirhams to 755 dirhams.
Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique advanced by six dirhams to 209 dirhams.
"Some 32,228 BNDE shares changed hands on the official market," a broker said.
It showed a net profit of 615.8 million dirhams ($66 million) in 1996, up 18.82 percent over the previous year.
ONA group, the country's largest private holding remained unchanged at 720 dirhams. ONA is expected to report an estimated 800 million dirhams net profits for 1996, a market analyst said.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest conglomerate which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, closed at 680 dirhams, up two dirhams from last Friday.
Newly-floated credit firm Credor rose to 655 dirhams from 650 dirhams last week.
Traded volume on the official market was 77.4 million from 69.6 million dirhams on Friday.
